newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall in lighter trade, seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall in lighter trade, seen mixed.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lower turnover on Thursday and analysts expected mixed trade on Friday amid speculation ahead of monthly earnigs reports, but said it was hard to predict where the whole market would move.
The main market's WIG index fell 0.6 percent, to 14,821.8, and turnover fell 20.6 percent to 86.4 million zlotys ($30.9 million) on both markets as 26 issues rose, 33 fell and 21 were flat.

"Tomorrow most firms are releasing their September earnings reports, so there will be some demand for selected stocks, but it's very difficult to say what effect it might have on the index," said Rafal Lis, an analyst at BGZ brokerage.
Traders were divided over the market's direction next week.
Some said the bourse still had growth potential and could find resistance at 15,200 or 15,600 points, especially if the September earnings proved strong.
But others saw the bourse falling to support at 14,400 or even 14,000 points, saying the market's 100-percent rise this year and forthcoming new issues could cool market sentiment.

They said the central bank's statement it would slow the zloty's crawling devaluation rate after year-on-year inflation fell in the future to 13 percent from the current 19.5 was good news for exporters but wouldn't affect the whole market.
Confectioner Wedel SA plunged 9.9 percent in a 3.5-million-zloty ($1.25 million) turnover after surging 9.9 percent on Wednesday, leaving traders puzzled by it's rapid swings.
They said industrial boilermaker Rafako SA fell 9.8 percent in 1.1-million-zloty ($0.4 million) trade on expectation of unspectacular September earnings.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 3.7 percent in a 18.3-million zloty ($6.5 million) turnover.
